item.title: Saturday, November 7, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the Portal North Bridge weekday cutover ends on 14 November, one week out, so anything depending on Midtown Direct access, site visits, inspections or closings gets materially easier from the 15th. Reprice your attached product now, because New Jersey condominium and townhouse inventory is up 22.5 percent year on year, the median is down 1.2 percent, and sellers are getting 99.5 percent of list rather than over 100. And stop underwriting to a cut: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly and Richmond's Tom Barkin both said this week that the next move is a hike, gradual but upward, even as the 10-year rallied on an equity panic. And three things for the world: the Democrats have taken both chambers of the United States Congress, with two Senate races still being counted, Mississippi by about 1,800 votes and Alaska by about 600. The president of Paraguay, Santiago Pena, has resigned after the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank locked roughly three million people, nearly half the country, out of their own money. And Como beat Lens 9-1 in the Champions League, equalling the biggest winning margin in the competition's history.

item.title: Friday, November 6, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: mortgage rates have fallen three weeks running, with Freddie Mac at 7.18% and the daily tracker at 7.17%, and FHA and VA thirty-year loans at 6.80% are a full 35 basis points cheaper than conventional, so the buyers shelved near 7.5% are worth a call today. National active inventory is up 7.4% year on year while new listings are down 7.5%, meaning the build is stalled demand rather than supply, and in the New York, Newark and Jersey City metro the price-cut share has risen almost three points to 12.6% while the median list price has slipped only 2.3% to $745,000, which makes this week's listing conversation about price rather than patience. Multifamily CMBS delinquency jumped 53 basis points in October while the overall Trepp rate held flat at 7.85%, so clients with multifamily debt maturing inside twelve months should start refinance conversations now. Also in this episode: the midterm aftermath and the fight to lead House Republicans, mined tankers in the Strait of Hormuz with Brent at $95, Herzog's coalition mandate in Israel, the Nasdaq's worst day in eighteen months, and Real Madrid's late win in Athens.

item.title: Thursday, November 5, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One, Freddie Mac's weekly survey prints today at noon Eastern with the 30-year coming off three consecutive declines from 7.24 percent, so anything unlocked gets a call this afternoon. Two, the Fed held its target range at 3.75 to 4.00 percent on October 28 and both dissenting votes wanted a hike, not a cut, so stop underwriting a December cut as the base case. Three, active inventory is up 7.4 percent year over year while new listings are down 7.5 percent, meaning your competition is ageing stock, so get sellers off summer comparables this week. And three things for the world. One, Democrats won both chambers of Congress on November 3, Hakeem Jeffries is in line for Speaker, the President is promising vetoes, and divided government begins in January. Two, markets liked it, with the Dow up more than 3 percent to 53,356 on the election result and a falling oil price. Three, a 7 million dollar film called You Can See Everything beat a 44 million dollar Warner Brothers picture to the top of the box office by 200,684 dollars. Also in today's episode: existing home sales at a 3.99 million pace, Manhattan third-quarter prices at a record on a 9 percent volume gain, Lightstone's 32.1 million dollar industrial buy in Newark Delaware, the collapsed Franklin Mills sale, McDonald's and Uber earnings, oil and gold, Real Madrid's 3-2 win at AEK Athens, Governor Sherrill's fight over Russian diesel at New Jersey's ports, and Mayor Mamdani's post-election victory lap.

item.title: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the thirty-year fixed sits at 7.30 percent on the Mortgage News Daily tracker against 7.24 percent on Freddie Mac's weekly survey, with the next PMMS print due Thursday the 5th, so quote the daily number and explain the lag before clients find the gap themselves. The FHFA announces the 2027 conforming loan limit in roughly three weeks, with 2026's set at 832,750 dollars, so pull every buyer sitting within 50,000 dollars of that line this week before the conforming-to-jumbo boundary moves under them. And stop letting anyone wait for rate cuts: the Fed held steady in late October and the live sell-side debate is one more hike in 2026, not a cut, so the buyer waiting for a five percent mortgage is making a decision rather than deferring one. Elsewhere: Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterms with Senate wins in deep-red states, Trump announced the United States will end roughly four billion dollars a year in military aid to Israel, Case-Shiller had national prices up just 2.1 percent year over year against 3.4 percent inflation, CoStar's 1.26 trillion dollar commercial debt wall keeps coming due, Cory Booker and Kathy Hochul both won re-election, and Real Madrid beat Racing Santander three-nil before heading to AEK Athens.

item.title: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: your rate relief is borrowed, not earned — Freddie Mac at 7.24% and the 10-year at 4.91% came from oil collapsing and Iran talking, not from the Fed, which held last week with two members voting to hike and roughly 85% odds priced for December; anyone sitting on a lock decision is sitting on a peace deal. Two: New Jersey is two markets and should be quoted as two — single-family at a $614,000 median, up 5% with 3.1 months of supply, against townhouse and condominium down 1.2% with listings up 22.5% and supply up 30%, so condominium price conversations happen this week, not next spring. Three: the 2027 conforming loan limit is due from FHFA within weeks — at $832,750 today that line decides jumbo versus conforming, so anything pencilled for January near it should be structured with the new number in mind. Also in this episode: US midterm Election Day, US strikes and simultaneous diplomacy in the Strait of Hormuz, Israel's hung Knesset, the expired Kherson truce, a split Monday tape with Marvell's $115bn move for Lumentum, and Real Madrid's 3-0 win at Racing Santander.

item.title: Monday, November 2, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: stop selling the Fed cut — both dissenters at the October 28th FOMC wanted a quarter-point hike, not a cut, and December is now priced above 80 percent for an increase; mortgage rates are easing on a softer long end and a compressing spread (30-year daily tracker 7.27 percent, Freddie Mac 7.24 percent, 10-year Treasury 4.93 percent), not on policy, so "wait for the Fed" is no longer a strategy. Two: New Jersey inventory is up 12.1 percent year on year to 22,746 homes while closed sales are down 5.8 percent and the median sits at 550,000 dollars — a buyer's market arriving quietly, so reprice listings before the market does it for you. Three: the title insurance fee waiver for refinancing borrowers in the October 22nd housing executive order is the nearest thing to free money in this brief — identify past clients above 7 percent who could be queued up for it. Also in this episode: pending home sales at a record low, down 7.3 percent in September; Case-Shiller national prices up just 2.1 percent, now below inflation; NAHB builder sentiment at 29, a 14-year low, with 43 percent of builders cutting prices; Manhattan median rent at a record 4,900 dollars against a city median asking price down 5.2 percent; Washington weighing renewed strikes on Iran; the US midterms tomorrow; Congo's Ebola outbreak past 5,000 deaths; a brutal Friday on Wall Street led by Intel down 28 percent; and Real Madrid's sixth straight win, 3-0 at Racing Santander.

item.title: Saturday, October 31, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One, the deadline: Tuesday's New York City ballot carries five questions and three of them change how property gets approved, with outdoor dining cut to a two-month process, bike and bus lanes fast-tracked, and construction permits consolidated into one digital hub while the Department of Buildings takes over all waterfront permits, so read those three before you vote. Two, quote rates carefully, because Freddie Mac has the thirty-year fixed at 7.24 percent, down eight basis points on the week but 107 basis points above a year ago, the daily trackers ran anywhere from 7.13 to 7.29 percent on Friday, and the Fed held this week with two members dissenting in favor of a hike, so sell the payment at today's rate rather than a cut. Three, New Jersey inventory is rising while Manhattan inventory is down about ten percent, so buyer leverage is improving in the suburbs and eroding in the city, and if any part of your book touches office, commercial mortgage distress reached 10.3 percent this month. And three things for the world: at least 35 attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz this month with the President briefed in person on military options against Iran including a naval blockade; a Russian drone killed at least 14 people on a railway platform in Dnipro while Ukraine quietly halted its strikes on Russian refineries until after the American midterms; and Binance says 6.3 billion dollars was stolen from it, the largest crypto theft on record, with investigators pointing at North Korea, as bitcoin fell to around 77,000 dollars and gold hit a twelve-month low.

item.title: Friday, October 30, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk this Friday. One: Freddie Mac's thirty-year fixed fell a second straight week to 7.24 percent, but Mortgage News Daily's tracker has it at 7.29 — quote clients the daily number, because that is what their lender will give them. Two: New Jersey inventory is up 12.1 percent year over year while closed sales are down 5.8 percent, so negotiating leverage has shifted and sellers have not noticed yet; start with attached product, where closings are down 6.6 percent. Three: CME FedWatch puts roughly 78 percent odds on a quarter-point Fed hike at the December 8th and 9th meeting, so anyone floating a rate into that week needs to decide before it, not during it. Also in this episode: the FOMC's 10-2 hold with both dissents running hawkish, record-low pending home sales at 66.0, New York metro prices up 6.2 percent, Israel's deadlocked election, 68 dead in Spain's rail disaster, the 6.3 billion dollar Binance theft, Alphabet's 12.6 percent drop, the MTA's widening deficit, and Madrid's 2-1 win at the Camp Nou.

item.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the Fed announces this afternoon with a ninety three percent chance of a hold and a six percent chance of a hike, so do not quote a rate to a client until you have read the statement; Freddie Mac's weekly survey lands Thursday morning and the daily index has been flat at 7.33 percent, so expect roughly no change and stop waiting on it for lock decisions; pending home sales just hit a record low while inventory is up 4.6 percent year over year and median days on market have stretched to 33, so rebuild your seller conversations around time and negotiating room rather than price. And three things for the world: Israel voted yesterday for all 120 Knesset seats with 61 needed to govern, and Netanyahu is fighting for his record and his legal future at once; Lula has won a fourth term in Brazil by nearly 4.5 million votes and Flavio Bolsonaro has conceded; and the ten year Treasury sits at 4.99 percent, which changes every conversation you have about money.

item.title: Monday, October 26, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the Fed decides Wednesday the 28th with PCE inflation Thursday the 29th, so any client sitting on a rate lock decision needs that conversation today. Two: the price reduction conversation is now backed by data, with 4.8 months of supply, 33 days on market and inventory up 4.6% year over year, and Lawrence Yun himself pointing to price cuts or incentives. Three: watch the permit mix rather than the headline, because single-family permits fell 4% while multifamily permits climbed to 503,000, meaning builders are rotating toward rental and next spring's for-sale pipeline is thinning. And three things for the world. One: Trump ruled out an Iran strike on Sunday, with the word "today" doing a great deal of work, while Qatari mediators are in Tehran. Two: office CMBS delinquency sits at 12%, worse than the peak of the financial crisis. Three: a $7 million documentary called You Can See Everything has now grossed $45 million. Also in this episode: September housing starts down 5.2%, existing home sales up 1.5% to a 3.99 million pace with a median price of $417,500, Friday's 653-point Dow drop on oil and AI capex nerves, Alphabet and Microsoft earnings Wednesday, Clayface topping the box office with $24 million, Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid with two from Mbappe, and New Jersey's general election one week from tomorrow.

item.title: Friday, October 23, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk: the Federal Reserve meets Wednesday 28 October and raised rates at its last meeting, so any buyer sitting on a decision should make it before Tuesday evening and any rate quoted after that needs re-checking; Freddie Mac broke a nine-week run of increases at 7.32 percent, the freshest good news since August, so use it in outreach today; single-family permits fell 4 percent in September and starts are down 7.4 percent on the year, so new-construction pipelines will thin by spring and resale inventory is worth lining up now. And three things for the world: Brent crude is above 111 dollars on fears of renewed strikes on Iran and mines in the Strait of Hormuz, a five-month high; Meta has been ordered to pay New Mexico 25 billion dollars over Facebook data privacy, the largest fine the company has ever faced; and Real Madrid have won all three of their Champions League games and travel to Barcelona on Sunday for the Clasico without Vinicius Junior.

item.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: PulteGroup reports third-quarter results this morning, and the incentive and rate-buydown spend is the best read we get on how much pain is in new construction. Two: Freddie Mac's weekly survey publishes today and the daily tracker went into it flat at 7.40 percent, so this is a plateau rather than a rally — with the FOMC minutes pointing to another increase and the 10-year at 5.13 percent, the case for locking rather than floating is about as strong as it gets. Three: pending sales fell 7.3 percent and months of supply is up to 4.8, so November and December closings are already thinner than September's — rebuild the pipeline this week and price listings to the slower market. And three things for the world. One: the Strait of Hormuz remains shut on Iran's terms, with oil flows at roughly 68 percent of pre-war levels and Brent touching 111.99 dollars, and nothing is expected to move before the US midterms on 3 November. Two: Meta posted a record 64.6 billion dollars of quarterly revenue and committed up to 145 billion dollars to AI infrastructure while absorbing a 10 billion dollar settlement charge. Three: Barcelona host Real Madrid on Sunday with six points between them at the top of La Liga.

item.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. First, today: September housing starts and permits at 8:30am Eastern and September pending home sales at 10am — pending sales is the freshest read on September contracts because existing home sales do not print again until 12 November. Second, 43 percent of builders cut prices in October averaging 6 percent, with 65 percent stacking incentives — pull new-development incentive sheets into your resale negotiations this week, because your sellers are competing with a 6 percent discount whether they know it or not. Third, the FOMC meets 28 October with the funds range at 3.75 to 4.00 percent and the market seriously debating a hike rather than a cut — stop telling buyers to wait for spring, and anyone with a lock expiring in three weeks should be having that conversation today. Two, France saw protests across more than 140 cities turn violent with more than 2,000 detained, and Macron has refused his interior minister's offered resignation. Three, Israel votes on 27 October, its first election since October 2023, with most polling showing Netanyahu's coalition short of a majority.

The daily thirty-year fixed is down twenty-seven basis points since October seventh to 7.37 percent, while Freddie Mac still prints 7.40 percent unchanged, so quote the daily number this week and tell anyone waiting on the Fed that the October twenty-eighth debate is hold-versus-hike, not a cut. New Jersey inventory rose again in September, so buyer leverage is returning in the mid tiers and anything sitting more than three weeks needs a pricing revisit. Housing starts and permits land Tuesday, and the FHFA sets the 2027 conforming loan limits in about five weeks, so clients hovering just above 832,750 dollars may land back inside conforming by waiting.
